title: F. Anthony Sampson

page_data.en:
F. Anthony Sampson
32 Rue Paul Henry
May 22, 1940.
282 (C)
22 5 40

Deputy Commissioner
Special Branch, SMP

Dear Sir,
This is to inform you that my name has been used, without
my permission, for a mailing address. This letter is not a
complaint, but is sent you for purpose of record only.
I have received an airmail letter from Chungking, addressed
to " Mr. A. P. Sampson, room 6, first floor, 19 Avenue
Edward VII, Shanghai ". This address is that of the
Shanghai Evening Post, where I worked until just over a fortnight
ago. There is no other Sampson on the Post-Mercury Company
staff. As far as I know, rooms are not numbered for address
purposes, although the doors may be numbered merely for aiding
identification of keys. The subject matter of the letter
received concerns me not at all: it is headed " c/o Mr. A. Cecil
Taylor, Chungking Hostel, 283 Kuo Fu Road, Chungking, May 4,
1940" and continues:
" Dear Sam, I hope you have received my letter which
reached Hongkong after you left, but was forwarded to you.
Please bring my letter to Dr. Sellett and take up the matter with
him, and let me know the results through your special channels.
I hope you will let me know right away what your expenditures
would be on your end as I would like to present the whole
proposition in concrete form before I take my trip to the South
Seas the beginning of June. That means, you must let me know
by return mail. With kindest regards, Sincerely yours
(signed) Eduard. "
Putting two and two together, I conclude that this letter
was destined for Mr. Sammy Chang, who is a director of the Ta
Mei Wan (Chinese edition of the Shanghai Evening Post, and who
has an office on the first floor of its premises. Mr. Chang,
known popularly as Sam or Sammy (as I am, too) recently passed
through Hongkong on his way back from Chungking. I gather that
the sender is Edward Ping-shuey Lee: I told this suspicion
yesterday to Inspector Crawford of your staff when I showed him
the letter, and confirmed it in a phone talk to Mr. Randall
Gould this morning, who said that Lee was fond of theatrical
flourishes of the false moustache type.
I complained to Mr. Gould over this wrongful use of my name
and told him that I was sending a copy of the letter to you.
Mr. Gould asked me please not to do this, said that I might get
Chang into trouble (or words to that effect) and that Chang
probably had nothing to do with this use of my name, Lee no doubt
being entirely responsible. I told Mr. Gould, nevertheless,
that I had a good name in this town, and that I was not going
to allow it to be used for any Chungking skullduggery. Mr.
Gould said that he would tell Mr. Chang to get in touch with
me, and that he would see that my name was not used again.
Mr. Gould's plea notwithstanding, I am sending you this
letter. I have nothing to do with Chungking nor its cash.
Yours faithfully,

(struck through: File confidentially)
Recd. 22/5
F. Anthony Sampson

F. Anthony Sampson
保罗·亨利路 32 号
1940 年 5 月 22 日。
282 (C)
22 5 40

致：
上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别分部副督察长

先生台鉴：
兹通知阁下，我的姓名在未经我许可的情况下被用作通信地址。此信并非投诉，仅送呈备案。
我收到一封从重庆寄来的航空信，收件人为“上海爱多亚路 19 号一楼 6 室 A. P. Sampson 先生”。该地址即《上海晚邮报》（Shanghai Evening Post）社址，我直至两周多前还在该处工作。《晚邮报-水星报》公司（Post-Mercury Company）职员中并无其他姓 Sampson 者。据我所知，房间并未编列号码用于通信地址，尽管门牌号可能仅为便于识别钥匙而设。所收信件的内容与我毫无关系；信头写着“转交重庆国府路 283 号重庆招待所 A. Cecil Taylor 先生，1940 年 5 月 4 日”，正文如下：
“亲爱的 Sam，希望你已收到我那封在你离开后抵达香港、随后转寄给你的信。请将我的信带给 Sellett 博士并与他商谈此事，并通过你的特殊渠道将结果告知我。希望你能立即告知我你那边所需的开支，以便我在六月初启程前往南洋之前，以具体形式提出整个方案。这意味着，你必须回信告知。谨致最亲切的问候，你真诚的（签名）Eduard。”
综合推断，我得出结论，这封信是寄给 Sammy Chang 先生的，他是《大美晚报》（Ta Mei Wan，《上海晚邮报》中文版）的董事，其办公室位于该报社 premises 的一楼。Chang 先生俗称为 Sam 或 Sammy（我也一样），最近从重庆返回途中经过香港。我推测发信人是 Edward Ping-shuey Lee（音译）：昨天我向贵处 Inspector Crawford 出示此信时表达了这一怀疑，并于今晨通过电话向 Randall Gould 先生证实了这一点，Gould 先生说 Lee 喜欢搞那种贴假胡子式的戏剧性花招。
我就这种冒用我姓名的不当行为向 Gould 先生提出抗议，并告诉他我将把此信副本寄给你。Gould 先生请我不要这样做，说这可能会给 Chang 带来麻烦（或类似意思的话），并称 Chang 可能与冒用我姓名一事无关，责任无疑完全在 Lee。尽管如此，我还是告诉 Gould 先生，我在此地享有良好的声誉，我不允许我的名字被用于任何重庆方面的鬼祟勾当。Gould 先生说他会通知 Chang 先生与我联系，并确保不再使用我的姓名。
尽管有 Gould 先生的请求，我仍将此信寄送给你。我与重庆或其资金没有任何关系。
此致
敬礼

（划去：机密存档）
1940 年 5 月 22 日收
F. Anthony Sampson
